title: Superpower #1: Focus and Commit to Priorities
coreMove: Make worthy alternatives lose so the surviving priorities can command time, resources, and buy-in.
sourcePressure: The first superpower makes focus and commitment explicit: choose what matters most and win enough participation that chosen priorities govern action.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not make focus sound like personal minimalism or commitment like verbal agreement.

sourceAnchors.name: focus and commitment
sourceAnchors.detail: The source frames focus and commitment as the first OKR superpower: choosing what matters most and earning stakeholder buy-in.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Focus cuts the list; commitment makes the shortened list strong enough to change calendars and tradeoffs.

hook: A team discovers OKRs in a conference room and suddenly gets aligned
A dashboard glows on a Monday morning and reveals the truth
A leader writes a goal on a whiteboard and everyone understands
opening with Superpower #1: Focus and Commit to Priorities as a definition rather than a pressure
counterintuition: Measurement is not bureaucracy, it is clarity
Goals are not dreams, they are systems
Accountability is not punishment, it is ownership
focus is not a mindset, it is a system
tryThisNow: Set a timer and write three goals

write one OKR without checking whether it changes behavior

home chore chart with vague family goals
